Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medicore is moving quickly on procurement and Legal asked us to confirm some specifics in the security exhibit before we sign the order form. High-level asks from our side: a short SOC 2 summary, a pen-test window (we need clarity on notice and staging access), and an evidence cadence for operational artifacts (logs, runbooks, attestation samples).

I've attached our security request spreadsheet with the items we typically look for. Can your team confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with: 30-day notice for pen tests, a sampling-based evidence cadence (we typically request weekly samples for the first 90 days), and a limited inspection scope (no access to production secrets)?

We'd like to map this into the MSA appendix / order form so procurement can move forward. I'm including Tom from IT for scheduling.

Thanks —
Natalie Price

Sean / Natalie —

Thanks for pulling this together. High-level legal approach and proposed redlines below (I attached a tracked-redline doc for your counsel to review):

- Scope limitation: inspection rights limited to systems and logs relevant to the service provided under the Order Form; no access to customer PII or Redwood production keys.
- Notice window: propose 45 days for on-site/interactive pen tests; 30 days for remote or coordination-only tests.
- Staging-first requirement: pen tests must be run against a staging environment that mirrors production feature-wise but without real customer data.
- Evidence cadence: agree to a sampling cadence for artifacts (weekly sampling for the first 60 days post-go-live, then monthly thereafter) and define a small canonical list of artifacts (SOC2 summary, change logs, incident runbook excerpts, limited log slices).
- Confidentiality & NDAs: any test reports containing sensitive Redwood internal info will be redacted and subject to an NDA / mutual non-disclosure clause.
- Liability carveouts & remediation timelines: add 30-day remediation window for non-critical findings and escalation path for high/critical issues.

Attached: MSA_redlines_SECURITY_EXHIBIT.docx (tracked). Happy to jump on the sync — I'm available Thu morning PT.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Natalie / Tom / Sean —

Thanks — adding some operational details from Security to help frame the options so procurement can pick what's practical. Attachments: SOC2_summary_2024.pdf, pen-test-template.pdf.

Pen-test window options (pick one):
1) Remote / Coordinated: 30 days notice, tests run against an isolated hosted staging environment we provide (no production credentials). Best for speed and lower risk.
2) Rolling inspection: 45 days notice, limited live sampling on production for a defined subset of endpoints, with a short maintenance window and a signed scope of endpoints. Higher visibility, more constraints.
3) Managed assessment: Redwood oversees the test and shares sanitized results; no customer credentials required. Good where customers want assurance without operational lift.

Evidence cadence (recommended):
- Onboard phase (0-60 days post-go-live): weekly artifact samples (SOC2 summary, architecture diagram snapshot, change-log excerpts, sample access logs — redacted).
- Stabilization (61-180 days): bi-weekly to monthly samples depending on ticket/incident volume.
- Long-term: monthly snapshots and annual full SOC2 report delivery.

Access model: ephemeral credentials for staging sessions, time-boxed viewer roles, and audit logging for every inspection. We will not provide any credentials that permit data exfiltration.

If Medicore prefers a 45-day notice instead of 30, we can accept that for Rolling inspection but recommend Remote/Coordinated for the initial procurement to avoid production risk.

Olga Petrov
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
